A1.justification: Both complete 27-page PDFs describe the same UPD/JUPD research. Text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–K support reliable comparison; appendix pages 14–27 are identical in extracted text and rendered appearance.

before.justification: v2 reports original reinforcement-learning evaluations on LBF, Overcooked-AI, and OGC, plus a 12-participant human-AI study and supplementary experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains the original benchmark evaluations, human-AI study, ablations, and supplementary experimental results.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–2, partner mixing and bias generation, learnability scores, PPO training, and the JUPD extension are unchanged. Figure 1's revised label does not introduce a method component.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same LBF setting, five Overcooked-AI layouts, 5×5 OGC, evaluation partner populations, and human-study population. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 1–3 and the LBF and human experiments. Section 6 changes 'CEC adaption' to 'CEC inspired baseline', but both descriptions specify random-level self-play without documenting a procedural change.

E3.justification: Training budgets, architectures, evaluation metrics, partner populations, and human-study procedures are retained. Section 6's generator clarifications do not establish a change to the experimental protocol.

E4.justification: The epsilon sweep, bias and learnability ablations, partner-selection dynamics, alternative learnability-function comparisons, and supplementary analyses are retained. Table 1's aggregate numerical revisions do not introduce a different analysis.

E5.justification: Seed counts, mean-and-standard-deviation reporting, and human-study statistical tests remain unchanged. Table 1 revises standard-deviation values without documenting a change in estimation procedure or uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes all seven aggregate standard deviations and six percentage gains relative to E3T; per-layout results, aggregate means, and rankings remain unchanged. UPD changes from 94.4±2.3 and +18.0% to 94.4±2.7 and +19.8%; SP's gain changes from -62.2% to -47.5%. Appendix Table 3 retains the old UPD values.

T1.justification: The game formulation, learnability definitions, convention-selection arguments, and computational-cost derivations in the main text and appendices are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about population-free adaptive partner generation, strong ad-hoc teamwork, joint partner-environment generalisation, and human collaboration.

C2.justification: Interpretations of ablations and convention-breaking dynamics are unchanged, as are qualifications concerning the human-study sample and dependence on efficient vectorised simulators. Discussion and appendix interpretations are retained.

D1.justification: Section 6 now explicitly states that DR-DR samples partners from the UPD generator and that all compared OGC methods share the same OGC-based level generator. These additions clarify implementation and controls; appendix hyperparameters, hardware information, and access instructions are unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds McKee et al. (2022), on environment and population diversity, to Section 3.2 and the references. It also describes the CEC comparator as an inspired baseline rather than an adaptation, modestly clarifying its relationship to prior work.

P1.justification: Editing is confined to the expanded baseline descriptions in Section 6, the added citation, and minor terminology and version-header changes. Section order and the broader narrative remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is lightly revised, including diagram elements and the label 'Partner-Level Learnability?'. Other figures and tables are retained, with limited placement and text-reflow changes; Table 1's structure remains the same.

improvement.justification: Table 1's revised percentage gains agree with its displayed means, improving numerical accuracy, while the generator and baseline-provenance clarifications improve precision. The correction is incomplete: appendix Table 3 still reports UPD as 94.4±2.3 and +18.0%, conflicting with Table 1's 94.4±2.7 and +19.8%. The net benefit is limited, with the underlying evidence and conclusions unchanged.
